text: Solve problems in quantitative aptitude reasoning using large numbers.

record_links.rationale: This worked example solves a large-number comparison problem by converting million, billion, and trillion expressions to digits and ordering them.

record.evidence_quote: Arrange the following numbers from the smallest to the largest: 50.5 billion; 0.055 trillion; 500.5 million
record.prompt_text:
Arrange the following numbers from the smallest to the largest:
50.5 billion; 0.055 trillion; 500.5 million
record.answer_text:
Step 1: Write all the numbers as digits only.

50.5 billion without the decimal point: $505\times1,000,000,000=505,000,000,000$
With the decimal point: 50500000000.0
Correctly grouped: 50,500,000,000

0.055 trillion without the decimal point: $0.055\times1,000,000,000,000=55,000,000,000,000$
With the decimal point: 55000000000.000
Correctly grouped: 55,000,000,000

500.5 million without the decimal point: $5,005\times1,000,000=5,005,000,000$
With the decimal point: 500500000.0
Correctly grouped: 500,500,000

Step 2: Write the numbers one below the other. Align them on the last digit.

$$
\begin{array}{r}
 50,500,000,000 \\
 55,000,000,000 \\
 500,500,000 \\
 \end{array}
$$

Step 3: Use the list from Step 2 to write the numbers in the required order.

From Step 2 is is easy to compare the numbers. Arranged from small to large:

$$
\begin{array}{r}
 500,500,000 \\
 50,500,000,000 \\
 55,000,000,000 \\
 \end{array}
$$

Therefore, the numbers arranged from smallest to largest are 500.5 million; 50.5 billion; 0.055 trillion.

record_links.rationale: This exercise asks learners to compare two large-number expressions using trillion and billion units.

record.evidence_quote: ### Exercise 1.11: Compare large numbers 1. Which number is larger, 0.08 trillion or 800 billion?
record.prompt_text:
### Exercise 1.11: Compare large numbers

1. Which number is larger, 0.08 trillion or 800 billion?
record.answer_text:
0.08 trillion without the decimal point: $8\times1,000,000,000,000=8,000,000,000,000$
With the decimal point: 80000000000.00
Correctly grouped: 80,000,000,000
This is 80 billion.

Therefore, 800 billion is the larger number.

record_links.rationale: This exercise asks learners to compare billion and trillion quantities.

record.evidence_quote: ### Exercise 1.11: Compare large numbers 2. Which number is smaller, 120 billion or 1.2 trillion?
record.prompt_text:
### Exercise 1.11: Compare large numbers

2. Which number is smaller, 120 billion or 1.2 trillion?
record.answer_text:
1.2 trillion without the decimal point: $12\times1,000,000,000,000=12,000,000,000,000$
With the decimal point: 1200000000000.0
Correctly grouped: 1,200,000,000,000

120 billion: $120\times1,000,000,000=120,000,000,000$

Compare the numbers:

$$
\begin{array}{r}
1,200,000,000,000 \\
120,000,000,000 \\
\end{array}
$$

Therefore, 120 billion is the smaller number.

record_links.rationale: This exercise asks learners to order million, billion, and trillion quantities.

record.evidence_quote: ### Exercise 1.11: Compare large numbers 3. Arrange the following numbers from the largest to the smallest: 3,600 million; 3 billion; 0.36 trillion.
record.prompt_text:
### Exercise 1.11: Compare large numbers

3. Arrange the following numbers from the largest to the smallest: 3,600 million; 3 billion; 0.36 trillion.
record.answer_text:
3,600 million: $3,600\times1,000,000=3,600,000,000$

3 billion: $3\times1,000,000,000=3,000,000,000$

0.36 trillion without the decimal point: $36\times1,000,000,000,000=36,000,000,000,000$
With the decimal point: 360000000000.00
Correctly grouped: 360,000,000,000

Compare the numbers:

$$
\begin{array}{r}
3,600,000,000 \\
3,000,000,000 \\
360,000,000,000 \\
\end{array}
$$

Therefore, the numbers from the largest to the smallest are 0.36 trillion; 3,600 million; 3 billion.

It is estimated that the population will almost double by 2050 to 400,400,000. Write this as a mixture of digits and words, so that it will be easier to read.
record.prompt_text:
### Exercise 1.13: Use large numbers to solve problems

2. During May 2019, Nigeria's population was recorded as 200,233,151.

a. Write the number in words.

b. It is estimated that the population will almost double by 2050 to 400,400,000. Write this as a mixture of digits and words, so that it will be easier to read.
record.answer_text:
a. Two hundred million two hundred and thirty three thousand one hundred and fifty one

b. Use a place value table to help you.

$$
\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
\text{trillion} &\text{hb} &\text{tb} &\text{billion} & \text{hm} & \text{tm} & \text{million} &\text{hth} & \text{tth} & \text{thousand} & \text{ h } & \text{ t } & \text{ u }  \\
\hline
 &  &  &  & 4 & 0 & 0 & 4 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0  \\
\hline
\end{array}
$$

The number can be written as 400.4 million.

record.prompt_text:
### Exercise 1.13: Use large numbers to solve problems

3. In 2018, the Federal Government of Nigeria estimated a total revenue of ₦6,607,000,000,000.

a. Write the number as a mixture of digits and words, so that it will be easier for the general public to read.

b. It was estimated that oil revenue would be ₦2.442 trillion of the total revenue and non-oil revenue would be ₦4,165,000,000,000. Determine which revenue is more, the oil revenue or the non-oil revenue.
record.answer_text:
a. Use a place value table to help you.

$$
\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
\text{trillion} &\text{hb} &\text{tb} &\text{billion} & \text{hm} & \text{tm} & \text{million} &\text{hth} & \text{tth} & \text{thousand} & \text{ h } & \text{ t } & \text{ u }  \\
\hline
6 & 6 & 0 & 7 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0  \\
\hline
\end{array}
$$

The number can be written as ₦6.607 trillion.

b. $2.442\times1,000,000,000,000=2,442,000,000,000$

$$
\begin{array}{l r}
\text{Oil:} & ₦2,442,000,000,000 \\
\text{Non-oil:} & ₦4,165,000,000,000 \\
\end{array}
$$

The non-oil revenue is more.

record.evidence_quote: ### Exercise 1.13: Use large numbers to solve problems 4. The side length of a cube is 1 m. a. Convert the side length to centimetres. Then determine the volume of the cube in cubic centimetres. Write the answer in words. b. Convert the side length to millimetres. Then determine the volume of the cube in cubic millimet
record.prompt_text:
### Exercise 1.13: Use large numbers to solve problems

4. The side length of a cube is 1 m.

a. Convert the side length to centimetres. Then determine the volume of the cube in cubic centimetres. Write the answer in words.

b. Convert the side length to millimetres. Then determine the volume of the cube in cubic millimetres. Write the answer in words.
record.answer_text:
a. 1 m = 100 cm

$$
\begin{array}{l l}
\text{volume} &=\text{side}\times\text{side}\times\text{side} \\
&=100\times100\times100\\
&=1,000,000\text{ cm}^3
\end{array}
$$

The volume is one million cubic centimetres.

b. 1 m = 1,000 mm

$$
\begin{array}{l l}
\text{volume} &=\text{side}\times\text{side}\times\text{side} \\
&=1,000\times1,000\times1,000\\
&=1,000,000,000\text{ mm}^3
\end{array}
$$

The volume is one billion cubic millimetres.

record.evidence_quote: ### Exercise 1.13: Use large numbers to solve problems 5. There are 31,536,000 seconds in one year. a. Calculate the number of seconds in ten years. Write the answer in words. b. Determine whether your previous answer is more or less than 0.3 billion.
record.prompt_text:
### Exercise 1.13: Use large numbers to solve problems

5. There are 31,536,000 seconds in one year.

a. Calculate the number of seconds in ten years. Write the answer in words.

b. Determine whether your previous answer is more or less than 0.3 billion.
record.answer_text:
a. $31,536,000\times10=315,360,000$

There are three hundred and fifteen million three hundred and sixty thousand seconds in ten years.

b. $0.3\times1,000,000,000=300,000,000$

The previous answer is more than 0.3 billion.

In 2018, the Federal Government of Nigeria estimated the following budget allocations to three of their ministries: ₦435.01 billion to Education, ₦444.43 billion to Defence and ₦269.34 billion to Health. record.prompt_text:
### Exercise 1.13: Use large numbers to solve problems

6. In 2018, the Federal Government of Nigeria estimated the following budget allocations to three of their ministries: ₦435.01 billion to Education, ₦444.43 billion to Defence and ₦269.34 billion to Health. Calculate the total allocation to all three ministries. Write the full number and give its name.
record.answer_text:
$$
\begin{array}{r r r}
 & 435.01\times1,000,000,000 & = 435,010,000,000 \\
 +& 444.43\times1,000,000,000 & = 444,430,000,000 \\
+& 269.34\times1,000,000,000 & = 269,340,000,000 \\
\hline
& &  1,148,780,000,000\\
\hline
\end{array}
$$

The total allocation is ₦1,148,780,000,000. It is one trillion one hundred and forty eight billion seven hundred and eighty million naira.
